bib.title: Drop the Hierarchy and Roles: How Self-Organizing LLM Agents Outperform Designed Structures

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Drop the Hierarchy and Roles: How Self-Organizing LLM Agents Outperform Designed Structures", Victoria Dochkina (MIPT), arXiv:2603.28990v1 [cs.AI], 30 Mar 2026. Preprint (IEEE-style format, no venue stated; data/code "upon acceptance", so not yet released). Single author. The acknowledgments say Claude was used for language editing.
COVERAGE: 40981 of 40981 chars read (all 10 pages, references included). No appendices exist. Extraction is clean. Tables and figures came through as text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Fixed-order "Sequential" beats centralised "Coordinator" on L3 tasks, consistently across three strong models.
  number: +14.1% Claude Sonnet 4.6 (0.875 vs 0.767), +12.4% DeepSeek v3.2 (0.829 vs 0.738), +12.2% GLM-5 (0.800 vs 0.713); all p<0.001
  setup: N=16 agents, L3 tasks, 120 tasks per model, synthetic tasks, LLM judge GPT-5.4, no multiple-comparison correction (the author argues the results survive Bonferroni)
  quote: "Claude Sonnet 4.6 0.875 0.767 +14.1% <0.001 / DeepSeek v3.2 0.829 0.738 +12.4% <0.001 / GLM-5 0.800 0.713 +12.2% <0.001"
  where: p5, Table IV
- Sequential beats fully autonomous "Shared" by 44% ("endogeneity paradox": neither maximal control nor maximal autonomy wins).
  number: 44%, Cohen's d=1.86, p<0.0001
  setup: pilot, N=8, GPT-4.1-mini, L3+L4 average, judge GPT-4o (the Series 1-2 judge). Q: Sequential 0.724, Coordinator 0.640, Broadcast 0.510, Shared 0.503. Resilience: Sequential 0.829, Coordinator 0.774, Broadcast 0.580, Shared 0.589. Balance: Sequential 0.510, Coordinator 0.478, Broadcast 0.363, Shared 0.369.
  quote: "The relative quality difference between the best (Sequential) and worst (Shared) protocol is 44%, with effect size Cohen's d= 1.86 (p <0.0001)."
  where: p4, Table III
- The proposed mechanism is the type of information each agent sees, not hierarchy. Sequential agents see predecessors' completed outputs. Broadcast gives intentions, Shared gives stale history, and Coordinator gives one agent's plan. This is an interpretation. The paper does not ablate it.
  number: none
  quote: "notintentions(which may change, as in Broadcast), nothistory (which may be stale, as in Shared), notsomeone else's plan (which may be suboptimal, as in Coordinator), butcompleted outputs"
  where: p4
- Protocol: Coordinator is N+1 LLM calls (1 sequential plus N parallel). Sequential is N calls, all sequential. Broadcast is 2N calls (two parallel rounds). Shared is N parallel calls.
  quote: "Coordinator (centralized, exogenous): Agent 0 acts as an external coordinator... LLM calls: N+ 1"
  where: p3
- Autonomy only helps above a capability threshold. Below it, fixed structure wins.
  number: Claude free-form 0.594 vs fixed 0.574 (+3.5%); GLM-5 free-form 0.519 vs fixed 0.574 (-9.6%)
  setup: Series 3 Block 6, N=8, freeform protocol. Three capabilities named for the threshold: self-reflection, deep reasoning, instruction following. These are asserted, not tested separately. The threshold rests on one strong and one weaker model.
  quote: "GLM-5: free-formQ= 0.519<fixedQ= 0.574 (−9.6%)—autonomy hurts."
  where: p5
- Among strong models, protocol choice explains more variation than model choice.
  number: 44% protocol vs ~14% model
  setup: the 44% is Sequential vs Shared. The ~14% is Claude vs GLM-5. These come from different experiments, so the comparison is loose.
  quote: "protocol choice explains 44% of quality variation (Sequential vs. Shared on the same model) while model choice explains ∼14% (Claude vs. GLM-5 on the same protocol)"
  where: p7
- Quality is flat from 4 to 256 agents, while cost grows slowly.
  number: Series 2, N=8→64: Q 0.954/0.952/0.955/0.949, cost +11.8%. Series 3, N=64→256: Q 0.964→0.967, Kruskal-Wallis H=1.84, p=0.61. 64→256 costs 4.6x with no quality gain.
  setup: Series 2 uses fixed roles, GPT-4.1-mini, 8,020 tasks. Series 3 Block 1 uses self-organisation, GPT-4.1-mini, L1 tasks only (easy, near ceiling), 6,000 runs. Quality is near ceiling, so flatness may hide nothing to gain.
  quote: "The Kruskal-Wallis test yields H= 1.84, p= 0.61— no statistically significant quality difference between 64 and 256 agents."
  where: p5, Tables V and VI
- Hierarchy forms but stays shallow.
  number: depth 1.0→2.0 from N=4 to 64; L1 1.22 → L4 1.56. About 45% of agents are idle at N=256.
  setup: depth is the longest dependency chain in a run. The Spectral Hierarchy (Exp3) runs stayed at depth 1.0 for all N.
  quote: "the system organizes into at most two management layers without external design."
  where: p6-7
- Roles are re-invented per task rather than fixed.
  number: 5,006 unique role names from 8 agents (5,010 at 64); 91% unique at N=64, 54% used once. Claude used 1,272 unique roles.
  quote: "Pre-assigning fixed roles to agents... is an anti-pattern that replicates human limitations onto entities that lack them."
  where: p6, p8
- Voluntary abstention: 38 of 60 non-contributing agents withdrew on their own under Sequential. Under Coordinator all 60 were excluded by directive. Claude abstains 8.6%, GLM-5 0.8%. The author says abstention correlates with quality (0.875 vs 0.767), but that is the same Sequential vs Coordinator gap and does not isolate abstention.
  where: p6, Fig 5
- Open-source is cheaper at similar quality.
  number: DeepSeek v3.2 reaches 95% of Claude's L3 quality (0.829 vs 0.875) at about 24x lower API cost. On L4, DeepSeek 0.629 vs Claude 0.594 (+6.0%, p=0.082, not significant). Tokens per task: Claude 37K, DeepSeek 47K, GLM-5 57K.
  setup: N=16, Sequential, 120 tasks per model, judge GPT-5.4.
  quote: "DeepSeek v3.2 achieves 95% of Claude's L3 quality (−5.5%, p <0.001) while being approximately 24× cheaper in API costs."
  where: p5, Table VIII
- Quality collapses with task complexity.
  number: L1 0.986, L2 0.992, L3 0.948, L4 0.614 (-37.7%, d=22.9)
  setup: N=32/64, GPT-4.1-mini, 1,800 tasks.
  where: p6, Table IX
- Model rankings flip between setups.
  number: Claude Q=0.689 in fixed-topology Block 2 (N=32) vs 0.875 under Sequential (N=16, L3). Block 2 ranked DeepSeek 0.978, GPT-4.1-mini 0.971, Claude 0.689, Gemini-3-flash 0.357.
  quote: "model rankings shift between experimental setups"
  where: p5, Table VII
- Shock resilience: quality recovers within 1 iteration after random agent removal, hub removal, and 25% model substitution.
  setup: N=32, complete topology, in the Spectral Hierarchy / Sparse Graph / Mean-Field models, not the protocol comparison. Resilience Index 0.959 / 0.919 / 0.844.
  where: p7
- Proposed three-ring constitutional governance: Ring 1 immutable (human), Ring 2 standards (human plus system), Ring 3 protocols (autonomous). The paper says it is theoretical and untested.
  where: p8

LIMITS
- The author concedes: the judge is an LLM, not a human; the judge changed between series (GPT-4o in Series 1-2, GPT-5.4 in Series 3), so absolute Q values are not comparable across series; tasks are all synthetic; Sequential latency is O(N); rate-limiting may have biased task completion; no formal multiple-comparison correction.
- Not shown: any real-world benchmark; human evaluation; ablation of the "completed outputs" mechanism; comparison to a true hierarchical-supervisor tree (Coordinator is a single flat planner with parallel workers); comparison to debate, voting or critic topologies; batched Sequential (future work); the four bio-inspired protocols (deferred to a companion paper).
- Confounds: the headline 14% and 44% come from different models, N, and judges. Coordinator's workers run in parallel without seeing each other's output, so Sequential's win may mostly reflect agents seeing prior outputs, not self-organisation of roles. The 44% pilot used a weaker model. The "fixed vs free-form" threshold result uses Q around 0.5-0.6, far below the 0.875 reported elsewhere. Sequential costs more wall-clock time. Series 3 Block 1 scaling uses L1 tasks, which are near ceiling.
- Dating: models are early-2026 API snapshots (Feb-Mar 2026), with temperature 0.7 for agents and 0 for the judge.

BUILDS ON
ChatDev (Chen, ACL 2024), MetaGPT (Hong, ICLR 2024), AutoGen (Wu, arXiv 2023), AgentVerse (Li, ICLR 2024), GPTSwarm (Zhuge, ICML 2024), Mixture-of-Agents (Wang, arXiv 2024), Scaling LLM multi-agent collaboration (Chen, arXiv 2406.07155, 2024), EvoAgentX (EMNLP Demo 2025), AgentNet (NeurIPS 2025), MAS-ZERO (NeurIPS 2025), ReSo (EMNLP 2025), HiVA (arXiv 2025), Hyperagents/DGM (Zhang, arXiv 2603.19461, 2026). Classical MAS and self-organisation: Wooldridge 2009, Shoham and Leyton-Brown 2009, Kauffman 1993, Bonabeau, Dorigo and Theraulaz 1999.

CODE: none.

FIGURES
- Figure 1 (p4): "Quality comparison across coordination protocols. Solid bars: pilot (N = 8, GPT-4.1-mini, L3+L4 average). Hatched bars: final (N = 16, Claude Sonnet 4.6, L3). The hybrid Sequential protocol achieves the highest quality in both settings." This is the single best candidate. It shows the four protocols on one axis in both setups. Figure 5 (p6, abstention) is the second choice.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. A tool-result file was truncated at 40000 chars on first read, and I fetched the last ~1000 chars separately. The text is complete. The "-5.5%" gap and the "95%" are the paper's own rounding, as 0.829/0.875 is about 94.7%. A few quoted lines have missing spaces from extraction, but the words are verbatim.
